## packages/drive/src/Http/Controllers/StorageController.php

SHA256 4e82233faffdf82e7166b19bdee9a3a677c8c5551e5f79c44104017cadb91ff7; bytes 4604.

```php
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace Vaulter\Drive\Http\Controllers;

use Illuminate\Contracts\Auth\Access\Authorizable;
use Illuminate\Http\Request;
use Vaulter\Access\AccessResolver;
use Vaulter\Drive\Http\Resources\StorageResource;
use Vaulter\Enums\Access\Ability;
use Vaulter\Exceptions\Access\PermissionDeniedException;
use Vaulter\Http\Controllers\Controller;
use Vaulter\Models\Drive\Drive;
use Vaulter\Models\Drive\Node;
use Vaulter\Repositories\Drive\NodeReadRepository;

/**
 * Read surface for a storage container (§2.1): its meta, the root node the client
 * opens into, and the used/quota accounting. Thin — the storage arrives
 * route-model resolved (swappable model bound in the provider); the Resource
 * shapes the response.
 *
 * Authorization (M2a / H.2): a storage's "view" maps to View on its ROOT node, so
 * show() guards Ability::View on the storage root through the AccessResolver before
 * returning the meta (mirroring NodeController's per-ACTION guarding); a denial 403s
 * via PermissionDeniedException. The root is resolved READ-ONLY (the BelongsTo on
 * root_node_id, never the provisioning StorageManager — a read endpoint must never
 * write), exactly as StorageResource resolves it for its ability flags.
 */
final class StorageController extends Controller
{
    public function __construct(
        private readonly AccessResolver $access,
        private readonly NodeReadRepository $nodes,
    ) {}

    /**
     * Guard View on the storage root before exposing the meta. Edge cases (matched to
     * NodeController's semantics):
     *
     *   - No root node (root_node_id null / the row missing): a storage is ALWAYS
     *     provisioned with its root folder in one transaction (StorageManager::provision),
     *     so a missing root is a corrupt/transient state with no node to authorize against.
     *     It 404s for EVERYONE — never leaking the meta (name, owner, quota) to a grantless
     *     actor — matching the package's deny-on-missing-root convention (ActivityController
     *     "a miss is a corrupt state and 404s" / DocumentNodeController::driveRoot abort(404)).
     *   - Null actor (unauthenticated): denied on a rooted storage — no actor ⇒ no grant
     *     ⇒ 403 (exactly NodeController::guard); on a rootless storage the 404 above fires
     *     first, so the meta never reaches an actor-less caller either way.
     *   - Open drivers (gate/spatie/azgard/null): $access->can delegates to the active
     *     host-role driver, so an open driver decides exactly as it does for the node
     *     listings — the database driver is never hard-coded here.
     */
    public function show(Request $request, Drive $storage): StorageResource
    {
        $root = $this->root($storage);

        if (!$root instanceof Node) {
            // No root folder to gate View on. Provisioning is transactional (the root is
            // born with the storage), so this is a corrupt/transient row, not a viewable
            // "unrooted shell": 404 for everyone rather than serving the meta ungated.
            abort(404);
        }

        $this->guard($request, Ability::View, $root);

        return StorageResource::make($storage);
    }

    /**
     * The storage root node, resolved READ-ONLY through the read repository (never the
     * provisioning StorageManager — a read endpoint must not write). Null when the
     * storage has no root_node_id yet, or the row is missing — matching how
     * StorageResource resolves the root for its ability flags.
     */
    private function root(Drive $storage): ?Node
    {
        if ($storage->root_node_id === null) {
            return null;
        }

        return $this->nodes->find($storage->root_node_id);
    }

    /**
     * Authorize an ability on a node through the AccessResolver (H.2), throwing a
     * 403 PermissionDeniedException when denied. An unauthenticated request is also
     * denied (no actor ⇒ no grant). Mirrors NodeController::guard.
     */
    private function guard(Request $request, Ability $ability, Node $node): void
    {
        $actor = $this->authorizable($request);

        if ($actor === null || !$this->access->can($actor, $ability, $node)) {
            throw PermissionDeniedException::forAbility($ability->value);
        }
    }

    /**
     * The acting authorizable for the request, or null when unauthenticated.
     */
    private function authorizable(Request $request): ?Authorizable
    {
        $user = $request->user();

        return $user instanceof Authorizable ? $user : null;
    }
}

```

## packages/drive/src/Http/Controllers/Uploads/S3MultipartController.php

SHA256 619145600800adcb133eedf6ddc4d5a8c34901c2256397d9db826fb311472f1b; bytes 8952.

```php
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace Vaulter\Drive\Http\Controllers\Uploads;

use Illuminate\Contracts\Auth\Access\Authorizable;
use Illuminate\Http\JsonResponse;
use Illuminate\Http\Request;
use Illuminate\Http\Response;
use Vaulter\Access\AccessResolver;
use Vaulter\Drive\Actions\Uploads\CommitUploadAction;
use Vaulter\Drive\Models\Uploads\UploadSession;
use Vaulter\Drive\Repositories\Uploads\UploadSessionReadRepository;
use Vaulter\Drive\Uploads\S3MultipartHandler;
use Vaulter\Drive\Uploads\UploadSessionManager;
use Vaulter\Enums\Access\Ability;
use Vaulter\Exceptions\Access\PermissionDeniedException;
use Vaulter\Http\Controllers\Controller;
use Vaulter\Http\Resources\Drive\NodeResource;
use Vaulter\Models\Drive\Drive;
use Vaulter\Models\Drive\Node;
use Vaulter\Repositories\Drive\DriveReadRepository;
use Vaulter\Repositories\Drive\NodeReadRepository;
use Vaulter\Support\Config;
use Vaulter\Support\Identity;

/**
 * The S3-multipart resumable-upload surface (§2.8 / D16 / M3a). Thin HTTP: it
 * resolves the route-bound session, AUTHORIZES through the AccessResolver (Edit on
 * the node for a new version, Create under the folder for a new file), records each
 * part and, on complete, assembles → BlobStore.commit (server-recompute sha256, H.3 —
 * the multipart ETag is never the content address).
 *
 *   POST uploads/{upload_id}/parts    → record (sign/proxy) a numbered part;
 *   POST uploads/{upload_id}/complete → complete-multipart → assemble → commit.
 *
 * A part re-upload REPLACES (the (session, part_no) composite primary key — S3
 * semantics).
 */
final class S3MultipartController extends Controller
{
    public function __construct(
        private readonly UploadSessionManager $manager,
        private readonly UploadSessionReadRepository $sessions,
        private readonly DriveReadRepository $storages,
        private readonly NodeReadRepository $nodes,
        private readonly AccessResolver $access,
        private readonly CommitUploadAction $commit,
    ) {}

    /**
     * Record one multipart part. The body is the part bytes; part_no / byte_offset
     * come from the query/body. A re-upload of the same part_no replaces it.
     */
    public function parts(Request $request, string $uploadId): JsonResponse
    {
        $session = $this->findSession($uploadId);
        $this->authorizeSession($request, $session);
        $this->assertContentLengthWithinLimit($request);

        $partNo = $request->has('part_no')
            ? $request->integer('part_no')
            : (int) $request->header('X-Part-Number', '1');
        $byteOffset = $request->integer('byte_offset');

        $result = $this->s3Handler()->putPart(
            session: $session,
            partNo: $partNo,
            byteOffset: $byteOffset,
            chunk: $this->chunkStream($request),
        );

        return response()->json([
            'part_no' => $result['part_no'],
            'size' => $result['size'],
            'etag' => $result['etag'],
        ], 201);
    }

    /**
     * Complete-multipart: stitch the recorded parts into the assembled staged temp,
     * then assemble → BlobStore.commit (H.3) and return the created node.
     */
    public function complete(Request $request, string $uploadId): JsonResponse
    {
        $session = $this->findSession($uploadId);
        $this->authorizeSession($request, $session);

        $this->s3Handler()->complete($session);

        // Inside the session's critical section (R-11) — the sweeper reclaims an Assembled
        // session too, and out here it was free to discard the staged bytes mid-commit.
        $node = $this->manager->commitAssembled(
            $session->refresh(),
            fn (UploadSession $locked): Node => $this->commit->execute($locked),
        );

        return NodeResource::make($node)->response()->setStatusCode(201);
    }

    private function findSession(string $uploadId): UploadSession
    {
        $session = $this->sessions->findByUploadId($uploadId);

        if (!$session instanceof UploadSession) {
            abort(404);
        }

        return $session;
    }

    /**
     * Authorize a request acting on an EXISTING session by its target shape: Edit on
     * the node for a new version, else Create under the destination folder — THEN
     * (F-P1.4-12) confirm the acting actor is the session's OWNER (see
     * TusUploadController::authorizeSession for the full rationale — the two
     * controllers share the identical guard).
     */
    private function authorizeSession(Request $request, UploadSession $session): void
    {
        $storage = $this->storageOf($session);

        if ($session->isNewVersion()) {
            $node = $this->findNodeInStorage($session->target_node_id ?? '', $storage);
            $this->guard($request, Ability::Edit, $node);
        } else {
            $parent = $session->target_parent_id === null
                ? $this->rootOf($storage)
                : $this->findNodeInStorage($session->target_parent_id, $storage);

            $this->guardCreate($request, $storage, $parent);
        }

        $this->guardOwnership($request, $session);

     * F-P1.4-12: see TusUploadController::guardOwnership — identical guard, shared
     * rationale, no shared base class to hang it on (kept in sync manually, exactly
     * like the rest of this authorizeSession/guard/guardCreate trio).
     */
    private function guardOwnership(Request $request, UploadSession $session): void
    {
        if ($session->created_by === null) {
            return;
        }

        $actorId = $this->actorId($request);

        if (Identity::stringify($session->created_by) !== Identity::stringify($actorId)) {
            throw PermissionDeniedException::forAbility('upload-session-owner');
        }
    }

    private function storageOf(UploadSession $session): Drive
    {
        $storage = $this->storages->find($session->drive_id);

        if (!$storage instanceof Drive) {
            abort(404);
        }

        return $storage;
    }

    private function rootOf(Drive $storage): Node
    {
        $root = $storage->rootNode()->first();

        if (!$root instanceof Node) {
            abort(404);
        }

        return $root;
    }

    private function findNodeInStorage(int|string $nodeId, Drive $storage): Node
    {
        $node = $this->nodes->find($nodeId);

        if (!$node instanceof Node || $node->drive_id !== $storage->getKey()) {
            abort(404);
        }

        return $node;
    }

    private function s3Handler(): S3MultipartHandler
    {
        return app(S3MultipartHandler::class);
    }

    /**
     * The raw part body as a STREAM, never a PHP string — see
     * TusUploadController::chunkStream() for the full rationale (VLT-REMED P5.2 review /
     * F-P1.4-04): the per-chunk ceiling used to sit BEHIND a `getContent()` that had
     * already materialised the whole body in memory.
     *
     * @return resource
     */
    private function chunkStream(Request $request): mixed
    {
        $stream = $request->getContent(asResource: true);

        if (!is_resource($stream)) {
            abort(500, 'Unable to open a stream for the upload part.');
        }

        return $stream;
    }

    /**
     * Refuse an over-cap part on its DECLARED length, before the body is touched — the
     * S3-multipart twin of TusUploadController::assertContentLengthWithinLimit(). The cap
     * (`uploads.max_chunk_bytes`) covers BOTH protocols: a part body is exactly as
     * unbounded as a PATCH body.
     */
    private function assertContentLengthWithinLimit(Request $request): void
    {
        $max = Config::uploadMaxChunkBytes();
        $declared = $request->server('CONTENT_LENGTH');

        if ($max <= 0 || !is_numeric($declared) || (int) $declared <= $max) {
            return;
        }

        abort(Response::HTTP_REQUEST_ENTITY_TOO_LARGE, "The upload part exceeds the maximum chunk size of {$max} bytes.");
    }

    private function guard(Request $request, Ability $ability, Node $node): void
    {
        $actor = $this->authorizable($request);

        if ($actor === null || !$this->access->can($actor, $ability, $node)) {
            throw PermissionDeniedException::forAbility($ability->value);
        }
    }

    private function guardCreate(Request $request, Drive $storage, Node $destination): void
    {
        $actor = $this->authorizable($request);

        if ($actor === null
            || !$this->access->canCreateInWorkspace($actor, $storage)
            || !$this->access->can($actor, Ability::Create, $destination)
        ) {
            throw PermissionDeniedException::forAbility(Ability::Create->value);
        }
    }

    private function authorizable(Request $request): ?Authorizable
    {
        $user = $request->user();

        return $user instanceof Authorizable ? $user : null;
    }
}
```

```php
use Illuminate\Contracts\Auth\Access\Authorizable;
use Illuminate\Http\JsonResponse;
use Illuminate\Http\Request;
use Illuminate\Http\Response;
use Vaulter\Access\AccessResolver;
use Vaulter\Drive\Actions\Uploads\CommitUploadAction;
use Vaulter\Drive\Data\Uploads\UploadInitData;
use Vaulter\Drive\Enums\Uploads\UploadProtocol;
use Vaulter\Drive\Http\Requests\Uploads\CreateUploadSessionRequest;
use Vaulter\Drive\Http\Resources\Uploads\UploadSessionResource;
use Vaulter\Drive\Models\Uploads\UploadSession;
use Vaulter\Drive\Repositories\Uploads\UploadSessionReadRepository;
use Vaulter\Drive\Uploads\TusUploadHandler;

use Vaulter\Enums\Access\Ability;
use Vaulter\Exceptions\Access\PermissionDeniedException;

use Vaulter\Http\Resources\Drive\NodeResource;
use Vaulter\Models\Drive\Drive;
use Vaulter\Models\Drive\Node;

use Vaulter\Repositories\Drive\NodeReadRepository;
use Vaulter\Support\Config;
use Vaulter\Support\Identity;

 * (Ability::Create in the target folder for a new file; Ability::Edit on the node for
 * a new version), and delegates every byte/state move to the UploadSessionManager /
 * TusUploadHandler / CommitUploadAction. No model writes live here.
 *
 *   POST   uploads               → create a session (returns Location + upload_id);
 *   HEAD   uploads/{upload_id}    → the authoritative Upload-Offset (resume point);
 *   PATCH  uploads/{upload_id}    → append a chunk; on completion assemble→commit;
 *   DELETE uploads/{upload_id}    → abort (staged temp + multipart reclaimed);
 *   GET    uploads/{upload_id}    → the session status (poll).
 *
 * The tus headers (Tus-Resumable, Upload-Offset, Upload-Length, Upload-Metadata) are
 * set per the protocol. H.3: the assembled bytes go through the SAME race-free
 * BlobStore.commit — the client sha256 / S3 ETag is never trusted.
 */
final class TusUploadController extends Controller
{
    private const string TUS_VERSION = '1.0.0';

    public function __construct(
        private readonly UploadSessionManager $manager,
        private readonly UploadSessionReadRepository $sessions,
        private readonly DriveReadRepository $storages,
        private readonly NodeReadRepository $nodes,
        private readonly AccessResolver $access,
        private readonly CommitUploadAction $commit,
    ) {}

    /**
     * Create a resumable session (tus Creation). Authorizes the target (Create under
     * the folder for a new file, Edit on the node for a new version), opens the
     * session and returns 201 with the tus Location header (the upload_id).
     */
    public function create(CreateUploadSessionRequest $request, Drive $storage): JsonResponse
    {
        $this->assertTusEnabled();

        $target = $this->resolveAndAuthorizeTarget(
            request: $request,
            storage: $storage,
            targetNodeId: $request->targetNodeId(),
            parentId: $request->parentId(),
        );

        $session = $this->manager->initiate(new UploadInitData(
            storage: $storage,
            protocol: UploadProtocol::Tus,
            targetParent: $target['parent'],
            targetName: $request->name(),
            targetNode: $target['node'],
            expectedSha256: $request->expectedSha256(),
            totalSizeBytes: $request->totalSizeBytes(),
            mimeType: $request->mimeType(),
            metadata: $this->mergedMetadata($request),
            actorId: $this->actorId($request),
        ));

        return UploadSessionResource::make($session)
            ->response()
            ->setStatusCode(201)
            ->withHeaders([
                'Tus-Resumable' => self::TUS_VERSION,
                'Location' => $this->locationFor($request, $session),
                'Upload-Offset' => '0',

     * point) plus Upload-Length. A second client resuming reads THIS, never its own

            'Upload-Offset' => (string) $offset,
            'Cache-Control' => 'no-store',

        // the manager so it runs INSIDE the session's critical section (R-11): a sweeper
        // may legally reclaim an Assembled session, and out here it used to be free to
        // discard the staged bytes mid-commit.
        $node = $this->manager->commitAssembled(
            $session->refresh(),
            fn (UploadSession $locked): Node => $this->commit->execute($locked),
        );

        return NodeResource::make($node)
            ->response()
            ->setStatusCode(201)
            ->withHeaders([
                'Tus-Resumable' => self::TUS_VERSION,
                'Upload-Offset' => (string) $result['offset'],

    public function options(): Response

            'Tus-Version' => self::TUS_VERSION,
            'Tus-Extension' => 'creation,termination',

        $maxBytes = Config::uploadMaxBytes();

    private function assertContentLengthWithinLimit(Request $request): void
    {

        abort(Response::HTTP_REQUEST_ENTITY_TOO_LARGE, sprintf('The upload chunk exceeds the maximum chunk size of %d bytes.', $max), [

     * then whitelist keys + cap value length (F-P1.4-08) — the merged map is what

     * v_upload_sessions.metadata without limit (U4.3/U4.4). Unknown keys are
     * SILENTLY dropped, not rejected: a tus client sending one extra vendor key
     * must not fail the whole upload over it.

     * @param  array<string, string> $metadata
     * @return array<string, string>

    private function sanitizeMetadata(array $metadata): array

        $maxLength = Config::uploadMetadataMaxValueLength();

            if (!in_array($key, $allowedKeys, true)) {

        foreach (explode(',', $header) as $pair) {
            $segments = explode(' ', trim($pair), 2);
            $key = $segments[0];

            if ($key === '') {
                continue;
            }

            $metadata[$key] = isset($segments[1]) ? base64_decode($segments[1], strict: false) : '';

    {
        return rtrim($request->getSchemeAndHttpHost().'/'.Config::routePrefix(), '/').('/uploads/'.$session->upload_id);
    }

    private function assertTusEnabled(): void
    {
        if (!Config::tusEnabled()) {
            abort(403, 'The tus resumable-upload protocol is disabled.');
        }
    }

    /**
     * F-P1.4-06: the CORE protocol requires the client to declare the resumable
     * version it speaks; a request that omits it (or names one this deployment does
     * not support) is refused with 412 + the version we DO support, never silently
     * accepted.
     */
    private function assertTusResumableHeader(Request $request): void
    {
        if ($request->header('Tus-Resumable') === self::TUS_VERSION) {
            return;
        }

        abort(Response::HTTP_PRECONDITION_FAILED, 'Unsupported or missing Tus-Resumable version.', [
            'Tus-Resumable' => self::TUS_VERSION,
            'Tus-Version' => self::TUS_VERSION,
        ]);
    }

    /**
     * F-P1.4-05: a tus PATCH body MUST be application/offset+octet-stream; anything
     * else (a stray text/plain, a misconfigured client) is refused with 415 BEFORE
     * a single byte is appended — never silently accepted as a valid chunk.
     */
    private function assertOffsetOctetStreamContentType(Request $request): void
    {
        $contentType = (string) $request->header('Content-Type', '');

        if (str_starts_with($contentType, 'application/offset+octet-stream')) {
            return;
        }

        abort(Response::HTTP_UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA_TYPE, 'PATCH requires Content-Type: application/offset+octet-stream.', [
            'Tus-Resumable' => self::TUS_VERSION,
        ]);
    }

    /**
     * Authorize an ability on a node through the AccessResolver (H.2); 403 on denial.
     */
    private function guard(Request $request, Ability $ability, Node $node): void
    {
        $actor = $this->authorizable($request);

        if ($actor === null || !$this->access->can($actor, $ability, $node)) {
            throw PermissionDeniedException::forAbility($ability->value);
        }
    }

    private function guardCreate(Request $request, Drive $storage, Node $destination): void
    {
        $actor = $this->authorizable($request);

        if ($actor === null
            || !$this->access->canCreateInWorkspace($actor, $storage)
            || !$this->access->can($actor, Ability::Create, $destination)
        ) {
            throw PermissionDeniedException::forAbility(Ability::Create->value);
        }
    }

    private function authorizable(Request $request): ?Authorizable
    {
        $user = $request->user();

        return $user instanceof Authorizable ? $user : null;
    }
}
```

```php
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace Vaulter\Drive\Http\Requests;

use Vaulter\Drive\Data\CopyNodeData;
use Vaulter\Http\Requests\VaulterFormRequest;
use Vaulter\Models\Drive\Node;

/**
 * Validates a copy request (§2.4): the source node is route-model resolved, the
 * destination parent (null = storage root) and an optional new name come from the
 * body. toData() takes the already-resolved nodes; an empty name override is
 * normalised to null so the Action keeps the source's name.
 */
final class CopyNodeRequest extends VaulterFormRequest
{
    /**
     * @return array<string, mixed>
     */
    public function rules(): array
    {
        return [
            'parent_id' => ['nullable'],
            'name' => ['nullable', 'string', 'max:255', 'regex:/^[^\/\\\\]+$/'],
        ];
    }

    /**
     * @return array<string, string>
     */
    public function messages(): array
    {
        return [
            'name.regex' => 'The name must not contain path separators (/ or \\).',
        ];
    }

    public function parentId(): int|string|null
    {
        return $this->nullableScalarId('parent_id');
    }

    public function name(): ?string
    {
        $name = $this->input('name');

        return is_string($name) && $name !== '' ? $name : null;
    }
```

```php
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace Vaulter\Drive\Http\Requests;

use Illuminate\Http\UploadedFile;
use Vaulter\Http\Requests\VaulterFormRequest;
use Vaulter\Support\Config;

/**
 * Validates a multipart upload (§2.4): the binary file plus an optional
 * destination parent, an optional stored-name override, and an optional target
 * node id for a new-version upload onto an existing file node.
 *
 * Unlike the move/rename/copy commands, the upload command (UploadFileData) is
 * assembled by DriveContext::upload()/uploadVersion() — they own the stream
 * normalisation that keeps the Action free of HTTP/PSR types — so this Request
 * exposes the validated file + targets and the controller delegates to the
 * DriveContext rather than building the DTO here.
 */
final class UploadFileRequest extends VaulterFormRequest
{
    /**
     * @return array<string, mixed>
     */
    public function rules(): array
    {
        $fileRules = ['required', 'file', 'max:'.Config::maxUploadKb()];

        // An empty allowlist stays permissive (the default); a configured list
        // restricts the upload to that mime set via Laravel's `mimetypes` rule.
        $allowedMimes = Config::allowedUploadMimes();

        if ($allowedMimes !== []) {
            $fileRules[] = 'mimetypes:'.implode(',', $allowedMimes);
        }

        return [
            'file' => $fileRules,
            'parent_id' => ['nullable'],
            'node_id' => ['nullable'],
            'name' => ['nullable', 'string', 'max:255', 'regex:/^[^\/\\\\]+$/'],
        ];
    }

    /**
     * @return array<string, string>
     */
    public function messages(): array
    {
        return [
            'name.regex' => 'The name must not contain path separators (/ or \\).',
        ];
    }

    public function uploadedFile(): UploadedFile
    {
        /** @var UploadedFile $file */
        $file = $this->file('file');

        return $file;
    }

    public function parentId(): int|string|null
    {
        return $this->nullableScalarId('parent_id');
    }

    /**
     * The existing file node to commit a NEW VERSION onto (§2.4); null = a
     * brand-new file upload.
     */
    public function targetNodeId(): int|string|null
    {
        return $this->nullableScalarId('node_id');
    }

    /**
     * Whether this upload targets an existing file node (new-version path).
     */
    public function isNewVersion(): bool
    {
        return $this->targetNodeId() !== null;
    }

    public function name(): ?string
    {
        $name = $this->input('name');

        return is_string($name) && $name !== '' ? $name : null;
    }
}
```

SHA256 d56198e5edcc58ea2cecfd6bea19d4e230658fa2c1d54f4946915a01fa84b3ab; bytes 4286.

```php
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace Vaulter\Drive\Http\Resources;

use Illuminate\Contracts\Auth\Access\Authorizable;
use Illuminate\Http\Request;
use Illuminate\Http\Resources\Json\JsonResource;
use Vaulter\Access\AccessResolver;
use Vaulter\Enums\Access\Ability;
use Vaulter\Models\Drive\Drive;
use Vaulter\Models\Drive\Node;
use Vaulter\Repositories\Drive\NodeReadRepository;

/**
 * The read shape of a storage container (§2.1): its meta, the root node the
 * client opens into, and the used/quota accounting the UI shows as a usage bar.
 * Read-only — it transforms an already-loaded Storage, never WRITES (it resolves the
 * root node through the read repository, never the provisioning StorageManager).
 *
 * @mixin Drive
 */
final class StorageResource extends JsonResource
{
    /**
     * @return array<string, mixed>
     */
    #[\Override]
    public function toArray(Request $request): array
    {
        /** @var Drive $storage */
        $storage = $this->resource;

        return [
            'id' => $storage->getKey(),
            'panel' => $storage->profile,
            'owner' => [
                'type' => $storage->owner_type,
                'id' => $storage->owner_id,
            ],
            'name' => $storage->name,
            'slug' => null,
            'root_node_id' => $storage->root_node_id,
            'disk' => $storage->disk,
            'storage_type' => null,
            'used_bytes' => $storage->used_bytes,
            'quota_bytes' => $storage->quota_bytes,
            'status' => $storage->status,
            'created_at' => $storage->created_at,
            'updated_at' => $storage->updated_at,
            // What the request actor may do on the storage ROOT (§2.6 / H.2),
            // resolved through the AccessResolver so the Vue client gates its
            // toolbar (open the storage, create folders, upload, manage).
            'abilities' => $this->abilities($request, $storage),
        ];
    }

    /**
     * The storage-root ability flags the Vue toolbar binds against, resolved through
     * the AccessResolver for the request's actor (§2.6 / H.2). Mapped to the four
     * frontend keys: view (View on root), create_folder + upload (Create on root,
     * AND the workspace-create gate), manage (Manage on root).
     *
     * Resilience: with no acting user OR no provisioned root node yet, every flag is
     * false — a read-only shell (the SAFE default; the toolbar advertises nothing it
     * cannot back). The Resource never WRITES, so a missing root is resolved as
     * "nothing yet", never auto-provisioned here.
     *
     * @return array<string, bool>
     */
    private function abilities(Request $request, Drive $storage): array
    {
        $actor = $this->actor($request);
        $root = $this->root($storage);

        if ($actor === null || !$root instanceof Node) {
            return [
                'view' => false,
                'create_folder' => false,
                'upload' => false,
                'manage' => false,
            ];
        }

        $resolver = app(AccessResolver::class);
        $flags = $resolver->abilitiesFor($actor, $root);

        $canCreate = ($flags[Ability::Create->value] ?? false)
            && $resolver->canCreateInWorkspace($actor, $storage);

        return [
            'view' => $flags[Ability::View->value] ?? false,
            'create_folder' => $canCreate,
            'upload' => $canCreate,
            'manage' => $flags[Ability::Manage->value] ?? false,
        ];
    }

    /**
     * The storage root node, resolved READ-ONLY through the read repository (never the
     * provisioning StorageManager — a Resource must not write). Null when the storage
     * has no root_node_id yet, or the row is missing.
     */
    private function root(Drive $storage): ?Node
    {
        if ($storage->root_node_id === null) {
            return null;
        }

        return app(NodeReadRepository::class)->find($storage->root_node_id);
    }

    /**
     * The acting authorizable for the request, or null when unauthenticated.
     */
    private function actor(Request $request): ?Authorizable
    {
        $user = $request->user();

        return $user instanceof Authorizable ? $user : null;
    }
}
```

## packages/drive/src/StorageManager.php

SHA256 a0c753a14221042a84a8ee214d20a15efbaefe0f34e4001ddedc02115f204160; bytes 4508.

```php
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace Vaulter\Drive;

use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Model;
use Illuminate\Database\UniqueConstraintViolationException;
use Vaulter\Database\VaulterDatabase;
use Vaulter\Drive\Events\StorageCreated;
use Vaulter\Enums\Drive\NodeKind;
use Vaulter\Models\Drive\Drive;
use Vaulter\Models\Drive\Node;
use Vaulter\Repositories\Drive\DriveReadRepository;
use Vaulter\Repositories\Drive\DriveStoreRepository;
use Vaulter\Repositories\Drive\NodeStoreRepository;
use Vaulter\Support\Config;

/**
 * Get-or-create a storage container for a host entity within a panel (§2.1), with
 * automatic root-folder provisioning. The polymorphic owner triple
 * (owner_type, owner_id, panel) is the idempotency key — guarded by the partial
 * UNIQUE index defineStorages adds, so concurrent first-touches converge on one
 * row (the INSERT loser catches the unique violation and re-reads).
 *
 * The storage's defaults come from the panel: disk from config storage.default_disk
 * and storage_type from the resolved Panel. A fresh storage gets a kind=folder
 * root node, and root_node_id is repointed at it once it exists (the schema leaves
 * that pair without a hard FK to dodge the chicken-and-egg insert order).
 */
final readonly class StorageManager
{
    public function __construct(
        private DriveReadRepository $read,
        private DriveStoreRepository $store,
        private NodeStoreRepository $nodes,
        private VaulterDatabase $database,
    ) {}

    /**
     * Resolve (or provision) the storage mounted on $owner within $panel.
     * Idempotent: a second call returns the same row.
     */
    public function forOwner(Model $owner, string $panel = 'default'): Drive
    {
        $existing = $this->read->forOwner(owner: $owner, panel: $panel);

        if ($existing instanceof Drive) {
            return $existing;
        }

        try {
            return $this->provision(owner: $owner, panel: $panel);
        } catch (UniqueConstraintViolationException) {
            // Lost the create race — the (owner_type, owner_id, panel) unique index
            // is the backbone; re-read the winner.
            $winner = $this->read->forOwner(owner: $owner, panel: $panel);

            if ($winner instanceof Drive) {
                return $winner;
            }

            throw new \RuntimeException(
                'Lost the storage provisioning race but the winning row is not visible.',
            );
        }
    }

    /**
     * Create the storage row + its root folder node in one transaction and repoint
     * root_node_id at the node.
     */
    private function provision(Model $owner, string $panel): Drive
    {
        return $this->database->transaction(function () use ($owner, $panel): Drive {
            $storage = $this->store->create([
                'profile' => $panel,
                'owner_type' => $owner->getMorphClass(),
                'owner_id' => $owner->getKey(),
                'name' => $this->defaultName($owner),
                'disk' => Config::defaultDisk(),
                'used_bytes' => 0,
            ]);

            $root = $this->nodes->create([
                'drive_id' => $storage->id,
                'parent_id' => null,
                'kind' => NodeKind::Folder,
                'name' => '',
                'size_bytes' => 0,
            ]);

            $this->store->setRootNode(storage: $storage, rootNodeId: $root->id);

            event(new StorageCreated(storage: $storage->refresh(), root: $root));

            return $storage;
        });
    }

    /**
     * Resolve the root folder node of a storage, provisioning a missing one
     * (defensive — a storage created outside this manager may lack a root).
     */
    public function root(Drive $storage): Node
    {
        $root = $storage->rootNode()->first();

        if ($root instanceof Node) {
            return $root;
        }

        return $this->database->transaction(function () use ($storage): Node {
            $root = $this->nodes->create([
                'drive_id' => $storage->id,
                'parent_id' => null,
                'kind' => NodeKind::Folder,
                'name' => '',
                'size_bytes' => 0,
            ]);

            $this->store->setRootNode(storage: $storage, rootNodeId: $root->id);

            return $root;
        });
    }

    private function defaultName(Model $owner): string
    {
        return class_basename($owner).' storage';
    }
}
```

## packages/drive/src/Support/Uploads/MagicByteSniffer.php

SHA256 97db17af16c912c580042c18746df4221511a85d4efd8ab49f300dc29e5c866d; bytes 2911.

```php
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace Vaulter\Drive\Support\Uploads;

use finfo;

/**
 * Content-vs-declared-mime sniffer for the assembled resumable object (§2.8 /
 * F-P1.4-11 / U5.5). A resumable commit must not trust the CLIENT's declared
 * mime — a file uploaded as image/png whose magic bytes are a ZIP (or a script)
 * is a type-confusion vector. The sniff reads the leading bytes of the assembled
 * object and compares the detected type against what the client declared.
 *
 * It is deliberately CONSERVATIVE to avoid false rejections of legitimate uploads:
 * it only rejects when BOTH the declared type and the detected type are concrete
 * (non-generic) and they disagree. An unstated declared type, or content finfo
 * cannot confidently classify (octet-stream / empty), is accepted — the sniff
 * disproves a lie, it does not attempt to positively classify every upload.
 */
final class MagicByteSniffer
{
    /**
     * Bytes read from the head of the object for magic-byte detection.
     */
    private const int SNIFF_BYTES = 4096;

    /**
     * Generic detections that carry no signal — neither a declared nor a detected
     * value of these can contradict anything, so they are treated as "unknown".
     */
    private const array GENERIC = [
        '',
        'application/octet-stream',
        'text/plain',
        'inode/x-empty',
    ];

    /**
     * Whether the object's leading bytes are consistent with the declared mime.
     * True (accept) when nothing is declared, when the declared or detected type is
     * generic, or when they agree; false (reject) only on a concrete contradiction.
     *
     * @param resource $stream a readable stream positioned at the object start
     */
    public function matches(mixed $stream, ?string $declaredMime): bool
    {
        $declared = $this->normalise($declaredMime);

        if ($this->isGeneric($declared)) {
            return true;
        }

        if (!is_resource($stream)) {
            return true;
        }

        $head = (string) stream_get_contents($stream, self::SNIFF_BYTES, 0);

        if ($head === '') {
            return true;
        }

        $detected = $this->normalise((new finfo(FILEINFO_MIME_TYPE))->buffer($head) ?: null);

        if ($this->isGeneric($detected)) {
            return true;
        }

        return $detected === $declared;
    }

    /**
     * Lowercase, drop any `; charset=…` parameter, and fold the jpeg/jpg alias so
     * equivalent spellings compare equal.
     */
    private function normalise(?string $mime): string
    {
        if ($mime === null) {
            return '';
        }

        $value = strtolower(trim(explode(';', $mime, 2)[0]));

        return $value === 'image/jpg' ? 'image/jpeg' : $value;
    }

    private function isGeneric(string $mime): bool
    {
        return in_array($mime, self::GENERIC, strict: true);
    }
}

```

## packages/drive/src/Support/Uploads/StagedUpload.php

SHA256 81031fe93a578bca040a1d3b0007033eb5efa8720722b2da55cab63910e9990e; bytes 13702.

```php
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace Vaulter\Drive\Support\Uploads;

use Illuminate\Contracts\Filesystem\Filesystem;
use Illuminate\Validation\ValidationException;
use RuntimeException;
use Vaulter\Contracts\Cas\StorageDriver;
use Vaulter\Drive\Exceptions\StagedUploadMissingException;
use Vaulter\Drive\Models\Uploads\UploadSession;
use Vaulter\Models\Drive\Drive;
use Vaulter\Support\Config;

/**
 * The staged temp for a resumable upload (§2.8 / H.3). The bytes accumulate on the
 * SESSION'S disk under a tmp/ prefix keyed by the upload_id, so they live next to
 * the eventual CAS objects (same disk, reclaimable by the sweeper) and never touch
 * the canonical CAS key until BlobStore.commit promotes them.
 *
 * A tus PATCH APPENDS to this temp; the assembled stream is read back from it and
 * fed to BlobStore.commit (which re-hashes it server-side — the temp's bytes, never
 * the client's claim). On commit OR abort the temp is removed.
 *
 * This is intentionally NOT the CAS ContentStore: the CAS stages to a LOCAL seekable
 * file for hashing, whereas this stages to the (possibly remote) session disk so a
 * multi-GB resumable upload survives across requests. The commit path streams this
 * back through ContentStore::stage, so the H.3 invariant (hash the local staged
 * file) still holds at the moment of commit.
 */
final readonly class StagedUpload
{
    /**
     * The in-memory ceiling for the assembly buffer before it spills to a temp file
     * on disk (§2.8 / F-P1.4-04): peak memory stays bounded by this, never the full
     * staged file, no matter how large the resumable upload grows.
     */
    private const int SPILL_BYTES = 2_097_152; // 2 MiB

    public function __construct(
        private StorageDriver $driver,
    ) {}

    /**
     * The tmp/ staging key for a session on its disk (§2.8). Keyed by upload_id so a
     * second session never collides, and prefixed tmp/ so the sweeper / an S3
     * lifecycle rule can reclaim abandoned staging in bulk.
     */
    public function keyFor(UploadSession $session): string
    {
        return "tmp/uploads/{$session->upload_id}";
    }

    /**
     * The resolved Flysystem disk a session stages onto — the session's storage disk,
     * or the install default when the storage relation is not loaded/present.
     */
    public function diskFor(UploadSession $session): Filesystem
    {
        return $this->driver->disk($this->diskName($session));
    }

    /**
     * The disk NAME a session stages onto (null → the install default disk). The
     * S3-multipart handler uses this to address its per-part objects through the
     * StorageDriver.
     */
    public function diskName(UploadSession $session): ?string
    {
        $storage = $session->storage instanceof Drive
            ? $session->storage
            : $session->storage()->first();

        return $storage?->disk;
    }

    /**
     * The current staged length on disk — the source of truth the manager reconciles
     * received_bytes against (a crashed PATCH must not advance the offset past the
     * bytes that actually landed). 0 when nothing has been staged yet.
     */
    public function size(UploadSession $session): int
    {
        $disk = $this->diskFor($session);
        $key = $this->keyFor($session);

        if (!$disk->exists($key)) {
            return 0;
        }

        return (int) $disk->size($key);
    }

    /**
     * Append a chunk's bytes to the staged temp at $offset (§2.8 tus PATCH). The
     * write is offset-aware and STREAMING (F-P1.4-04): the already-staged bytes up
     * to the authoritative offset are streamed into a spill-to-disk assembly buffer
     * followed by the new chunk, and the result is written back — the full staged
     * file is NEVER read into a PHP string, so peak memory stays bounded by the
     * spill ceiling regardless of upload size. A per-chunk ceiling is enforced
     * BEFORE any bytes are staged. Returns the new staged length.
     *
     * FAIL-CLOSED (VLT-REMED P5.2 / R-03): a positive $offset with NO staged object is
     * an impossible state — the bytes it names were accepted and acknowledged. It only
     * happens when the object was removed underneath us (a concurrent sweep/abort — see
     * R-02 — or an out-of-band bucket cleanup). Continuing would write the new chunk
     * alone, drop the already-accepted prefix and hand the client a REGRESSED offset:
     * a corrupted file with no error anywhere. We refuse instead.
     *
     * @param resource $chunk
     */
    public function append(UploadSession $session, mixed $chunk, int $offset): int
    {
        $this->assertChunkWithinLimit($chunk);

        $disk = $this->diskFor($session);
        $key = $this->keyFor($session);

        if ($offset > 0 && !$disk->exists($key)) {
            throw StagedUploadMissingException::forSession($session->upload_id, $offset);
        }

        // A spill-to-disk buffer: it holds up to SPILL_BYTES in RAM then transparently
        // spills to a temp file, so assembling a multi-GB staged file peaks at the
        // ceiling, not the file size (F-P1.4-04).
        $buffer = fopen('php://temp/maxmemory:'.self::SPILL_BYTES, 'r+b');

        if ($buffer === false) {
            throw new RuntimeException('Unable to open an assembly buffer for the upload chunk.');
        }

        try {
            // Honour the authoritative offset: stream only the bytes we already hold
            // up to it (anything past it is dropped — the server, not the client, owns
            // the resume point, H.3 / §2.8). Streamed, never materialised as a string.
            // The object's existence is guaranteed above (fail-closed, R-03).
            if ($offset > 0) {
                $existing = $disk->readStream($key);

                if (is_resource($existing)) {
                    try {
                        stream_copy_to_stream($existing, $buffer, $offset);
                    } finally {
                        fclose($existing);
                    }
                }
            }

            $this->copyChunkWithinLimit($chunk, $buffer);

            $size = ftell($buffer);
            rewind($buffer);
            $disk->writeStream($key, $buffer);
        } finally {
            fclose($buffer);
        }

        return is_int($size) ? $size : 0;
    }

    /**
     * Whether $chunk's bytes are IDENTICAL to what already sits on the staged temp
     * at [$offset, $offset+len($chunk)) (§2.8 / F-P1.4-02, N3 C6): the ONLY case tus
     * permits treating an `offset < server` PATCH as an idempotent retransmit rather
     * than a 409 Conflict. A chunk longer than what is already staged, or whose
     * bytes disagree anywhere in the overlap, is NOT a match — the caller rejects it.
     * The chunk is read into memory (bounded by the same per-request body size the
     * controller already materialises for every PATCH — no new ceiling introduced);
     * the ALREADY-staged range is read back in bounded blocks, never the whole file.
     *
     * @param resource $chunk
     */
    public function rangeMatches(UploadSession $session, mixed $chunk, int $offset): bool
    {
        $chunkBytes = stream_get_contents($chunk);

        if ($chunkBytes === false) {
            return false;
        }

        $length = strlen($chunkBytes);

        if ($length === 0) {
            // A zero-length retransmit trivially matches whatever already sits there.
            return true;
        }

        $disk = $this->diskFor($session);
        $key = $this->keyFor($session);

        if (!$disk->exists($key) || $disk->size($key) < $offset + $length) {
            return false;
        }

        $existing = $disk->readStream($key);

        if (!is_resource($existing)) {
            return false;
        }

        try {
            if ($offset > 0) {
                $this->discardBytes($existing, $offset);
            }

            return fread($existing, $length) === $chunkBytes;
        } finally {
            fclose($existing);
        }
    }

    /**
     * Advance a (possibly non-seekable) stream past $bytes without materialising
     * them as one block — read-and-drop in bounded chunks so the discard itself
     * never grows memory past the spill ceiling, however far into the staged file
     * $bytes reaches.
     *
     * @param resource $stream
     */
    private function discardBytes(mixed $stream, int $bytes): void
    {
        $remaining = $bytes;

        while ($remaining > 0 && !feof($stream)) {
            $read = fread($stream, min($remaining, self::SPILL_BYTES));

            if ($read === false || $read === '') {
                break;
            }

            $remaining -= strlen($read);
        }
    }

    /**
     * Reject a PATCH chunk larger than the per-chunk hard ceiling BEFORE any bytes are
     * staged (§2.8 / F-P1.4-04 / U3.3): an unbounded single PATCH is a memory/IO DoS
     * vector. This is `uploads.max_chunk_bytes` — the hard cap — NOT `chunk_size`, which
     * is only the advertised HINT. 0 disables the cap; the shipped default does NOT (it
     * is 64 MiB — VLT-REMED P5.2 review).
     *
     * This is the CHEAP pre-check and it only sees a stat-able stream (a seekable temp).
     * The real request body is `php://input`, whose fstat size is 0 — for that one the
     * barrier is {@see copyChunkWithinLimit()}, on the copy itself. Both are needed: the
     * caller may hand us either.
     *
     * @param resource $chunk
     */
    private function assertChunkWithinLimit(mixed $chunk): void
    {
        $max = Config::uploadMaxChunkBytes();

        if ($max <= 0) {
            return;
        }

        $stat = is_resource($chunk) ? fstat($chunk) : false;
        $size = is_array($stat) ? (int) $stat['size'] : 0;

        if ($size > $max) {
            $this->rejectOversizeChunk($size, $max);
        }
    }

    /**
     * Copy the chunk into the assembly buffer, refusing to read past the per-chunk ceiling
     * (VLT-REMED P5.2 review). A body whose length we cannot know up front (`php://input`
     * under chunked transfer-encoding, or any non-stat-able stream) would otherwise slip
     * past {@see assertChunkWithinLimit()} entirely — the check that the docblock there
     * promises happens "BEFORE any bytes are staged" — and stream in unbounded. We read at
     * most $max+1 bytes: one byte past the ceiling is already proof it was crossed, and the
     * refusal still happens before `writeStream()`, so nothing is staged.
     *
     * @param resource $chunk
     * @param resource $buffer
     */
    private function copyChunkWithinLimit(mixed $chunk, mixed $buffer): void
    {
        $max = Config::uploadMaxChunkBytes();

        if ($max <= 0) {
            stream_copy_to_stream($chunk, $buffer);

            return;
        }

        $copied = stream_copy_to_stream($chunk, $buffer, $max + 1);

        if ($copied !== false && $copied > $max) {
            // We stopped reading at the ceiling, so the true body length is unknown — say
            // only what we KNOW, never a size we did not measure.
            $this->rejectOversizeChunk(null, $max);
        }
    }

    private function rejectOversizeChunk(?int $size, int $max): never
    {
        $measured = $size === null ? 'The upload chunk' : "The upload chunk of {$size} bytes";

        throw ValidationException::withMessages([
            'chunk' => "{$measured} exceeds the maximum chunk size of {$max} bytes.",
        ]);
    }

    /**
     * Overwrite the staged temp with $bytes in one shot (§2.8 S3-multipart assemble):
     * the multipart parts have been stitched into the assembled object, which is
     * written here so the commit path can stream it through ContentStore::stage and
     * re-hash it server-side.
     */
    public function write(UploadSession $session, string $bytes): int
    {
        $disk = $this->diskFor($session);
        $disk->put($this->keyFor($session), $bytes);

        return strlen($bytes);
    }

    /**
     * Stream an assembled upload into the staged object without materialising the
     * complete payload in PHP memory.
     *
     * @param resource $stream
     */
    public function writeStream(UploadSession $session, mixed $stream): int
    {
        if (!is_resource($stream)) {
            throw new RuntimeException('Unable to stage upload from a non-resource stream.');
        }

        if (!$this->driver->put($this->keyFor($session), $stream, $this->diskName($session))) {
            throw new RuntimeException("Unable to write staged upload [{$session->upload_id}].");
        }

        return $this->size($session);
    }

    /**
     * A read stream over the staged temp, or null when nothing is staged. The commit
     * path feeds this to BlobStore.commit (which stages it locally and re-hashes —
     * H.3).
     *
     * @return resource|null
     */
    public function readStream(UploadSession $session): mixed
    {
        $disk = $this->diskFor($session);
        $key = $this->keyFor($session);

        if (!$disk->exists($key)) {
            return null;
        }

        $stream = $disk->readStream($key);

        return is_resource($stream) ? $stream : null;
    }

    /**
     * Remove the staged temp (§2.8) — called on commit AND on abort/expire so an
     * abandoned upload never leaves bytes behind. Idempotent.
     */
    public function discard(UploadSession $session): void
    {
        $disk = $this->diskFor($session);
        $key = $this->keyFor($session);

        if ($disk->exists($key)) {
            $disk->delete($key);
        }
    }
}
```

## packages/drive/src/ValueObjects/WorkspaceRef.php

SHA256 120e700ad9f1887630857c877b46d31cebcd5ad4b2ed711b698b86cfe0151274; bytes 628.

```php
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace Vaulter\Drive\ValueObjects;

/**
 * A polymorphic reference to the host entity that owns a set of documents
 * (organization, project, deal, user…).
 */
final readonly class WorkspaceRef
{
    public function __construct(
        public string $type,
        public int|string $id,
    ) {}

    public static function make(string $type, int|string $id): self
    {
        return new self(type: $type, id: $id);
    }

    public function equals(self $other): bool
    {
        return $this->type === $other->type
            && (string) $this->id === (string) $other->id;
    }
}
```

+`CompleteUploadAction` is the **one place** staged bytes cross into the Drive, and it does so

 ```json
new file mode 100644
index 00000000..6b5cd3ab
--- /dev/null
+++ b/packages/drive/src/DriveHandleFactory.php
@@ -0,0 +1,60 @@
+<?php
+
+declare(strict_types=1);
+
+namespace Vaulter\Drive;
+
+use Illuminate\Contracts\Container\Container;
+use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Model;
+use Vaulter\Contracts\Drive\DriveHandle as DriveHandleContract;
+use Vaulter\Contracts\Drive\DriveHandleFactory as DriveHandleFactoryContract;
+use Vaulter\Drive\Actions\Files\IngestFileAction;
+use Vaulter\Drive\Actions\Nodes\CopyNodeAction;
+use Vaulter\Drive\Actions\Nodes\CreateFolderAction;
+use Vaulter\Drive\Actions\Nodes\MoveNodeAction;
+use Vaulter\Drive\Actions\Nodes\RenameNodeAction;
+use Vaulter\Drive\Actions\Trash\PurgeNodeAction;
+use Vaulter\Drive\Actions\Trash\RestoreNodeAction;
+use Vaulter\Drive\Actions\Trash\TrashNodeAction;
+use Vaulter\Models\Drive\Drive;
+use Vaulter\Profiles\ProfileRegistry;
+use Vaulter\Repositories\Drive\NodeReadRepository;
+
+/**
+ * The vaulter-drive implementation of the core {@see DriveHandleFactory} seam
+ * (P2 #5 / ADR-0015). It wires the DriveProvisioner, NodeReadRepository and the eight
+ * Drive Actions into a {@see DriveHandle}, so `Vaulter::for()` / `Vaulter::forStorage()`
+ * (defined in core's VaulterManager) return a working handle without core ever
+ * referencing a Drive class. Bound to the contract by VaulterDriveServiceProvider.
+ */
+final readonly class DriveHandleFactory implements DriveHandleFactoryContract
+{
+    public function __construct(
+        private Container $container,
+    ) {}
+
+    public function forOwner(Model $entity, string $panel): DriveHandleContract
+    {
+        $storage = $this->container->make(DriveProvisioner::class)->forOwner(owner: $entity, panel: $panel);
+
+        return $this->forStorage($storage);
+    }
+
+    public function forStorage(Drive $storage): DriveHandleContract
+    {
+        return new DriveHandle(
+            storage: $storage,
+            profiles: $this->container->make(ProfileRegistry::class),

-<?php
-

-
-namespace Vaulter\Drive;
-
-use Illuminate\Contracts\Container\Container;
-use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Model;
-use Vaulter\Contracts\Drive\DriveHandle;
-use Vaulter\Contracts\Drive\DriveHandleFactory;
-use Vaulter\Drive\Actions\CopyNodeAction;
-use Vaulter\Drive\Actions\CreateFolderAction;
-use Vaulter\Drive\Actions\ForceDeleteNodeAction;
-use Vaulter\Drive\Actions\MoveNodeAction;
-use Vaulter\Drive\Actions\RenameNodeAction;
-use Vaulter\Drive\Actions\RestoreNodeAction;
-use Vaulter\Drive\Actions\TrashNodeAction;
-use Vaulter\Drive\Actions\UploadFileAction;
-use Vaulter\Models\Drive\Drive;
-use Vaulter\Repositories\Drive\NodeReadRepository;
-
-/**
- * The vaulter-drive implementation of the core {@see DriveHandleFactory} seam
- * (P2 #5 / ADR-0015). It wires the StorageManager, NodeReadRepository and the eight
- * Drive Actions into a {@see DriveContext}, so `Vaulter::for()` / `Vaulter::forStorage()`
- * (defined in core's VaulterManager) return a working handle without core ever
- * referencing a Drive class. Bound to the contract by VaulterDriveServiceProvider.
- */
-final readonly class DriveManager implements DriveHandleFactory
-{
-    public function __construct(
-        private Container $container,
-    ) {}
-
-    public function forOwner(Model $entity, string $panel): DriveHandle
-    {
-        $storage = $this->container->make(StorageManager::class)->forOwner(owner: $entity, panel: $panel);
-
-        return $this->forStorage($storage);
-    }
-
-    public function forStorage(Drive $storage): DriveHandle
-    {
-        return new DriveContext(
-            storage: $storage,
-            panel: $storage->profile,
-            storages: $this->container->make(StorageManager::class),
-            nodes: $this->container->make(NodeReadRepository::class),
-            createFolder: $this->container->make(CreateFolderAction::class),
-            uploadFile: $this->container->make(UploadFileAction::class),
-            moveNode: $this->container->make(MoveNodeAction::class),
-            renameNode: $this->container->make(RenameNodeAction::class),
-            copyNode: $this->container->make(CopyNodeAction::class),
-            trashNode: $this->container->make(TrashNodeAction::class),
-            restoreNode: $this->container->make(RestoreNodeAction::class),
-            forceDeleteNode: $this->container->make(ForceDeleteNodeAction::class),
-        );
-    }
-}

-<?php

-declare(strict_types=1);
-
-namespace Vaulter\Drive\Enums;
-
-use Vaulter\Attributes\Label;
-use Vaulter\Support\Concerns\HasLabel;
-
-enum BulkAction: string
-{
-    use HasLabel;
-
-    #[Label('Delete')]
-    case Delete = 'delete';
-
-    #[Label('Restore')]
-    case Restore = 'restore';
-
-    #[Label('Move')]
-    case Move = 'move';
-
-    #[Label('Delete permanently')]
-    case ForceDelete = 'force-delete';
-
-    /** The document ability required to perform this action. */
-    public function ability(): string
-    {
-        return match ($this) {
-            self::Delete => 'delete',
-            self::Move => 'edit',
-            self::Restore, self::ForceDelete => 'manage',
-        };
-    }
-
-    /** Whether the action operates on trashed (soft-deleted) documents. */
-    public function operatesOnTrash(): bool
-    {
-        return $this === self::Restore || $this === self::ForceDelete;
-    }
-
-    /**
-     * @return list<string>
-     */
-    public static function values(): array
-    {
-        return array_map(static fn (self $action): string => $action->value, self::cases());
-    }
-}
```
